stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured $190 million in Series C funding, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The cash is aimed at enhancing co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, which the DoD seems to be particularly interested in. This funding round underscores the growing importance of security in space as geopolitical tensions rise.
stories.soWhat: If the DoD is pulling through for True Anomaly, it suggests they see co-orbital threats as a real concern—not just a future worry.

stories.head: Voyager gets $16.5M DARPA boost for propellant tech
stories.body: Voyager has clinched a $16.5 million contract from DARPA focused on solid rocket propellant technology. This contract highlights the ongoing need for improved propulsion systems, particularly as competition in the defense sector heats up. It seems even rocket science needs a little extra funding to keep pace with modern demands.
stories.soWhat: The fact that DARPA is investing in propellant technology suggests they’re not just looking for quick fixes but are preparing for a long-term strategy in aerospace capabilities.

stories.head: European smallsat sector struggles despite budget boosts
stories.body: Despite a surge in military budgets, Europe's small satellite industry remains bogged down by regulatory hurdles and capital access issues. Panelists at a recent conference warned that without addressing these bureaucratic challenges, the potential benefits of increased defense spending may remain unrealized. It's a classic case of having the money but not being able to spend it effectively.
stories.soWhat: If Europe can't clear these regulatory hurdles, they risk losing ground to more agile competitors in the U.S. and Asia.

watchlist.title: Watch for DARPA's next funding trends
watchlist.body: With Voyager's recent contract, DARPA might be doubling down on propulsion technology, potentially signaling future funding opportunities.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on European defense budgets
watchlist.body: As military budgets rise, any shifts in regulatory frameworks could either unlock or stifle the smallsat sector's growth.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next moves post-funding
watchlist.body: Investors will be keen to see how True Anomaly utilizes its new funding to ramp up capabilities in co-orbital security.

watchlist.title: Impact of SpaceX's valuation on the market
watchlist.body: SpaceX's secondary market valuation at $470 billion could influence investor sentiment and funding dynamics across the space sector.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
